verified_hypothesis.finding: Python assignment runs late RNA update whenever pointer conversion/setter produced no error because Object.data has an update callback. The void setter does not signal whether it changed data. Edit and null-nonempty silent returns therefore do not suppress the subsequent relation/geometry update. A same-pointer assignment also continues, and is not a native Mesh no-op.

Object.data callback always calls DEG_relations_tag_update(bmain), DEG_id_tag_update(Object owner,ID_RECALC_GEOMETRY) and native draw notifier. Generic RNA update additionally publishes message bus and tags eligible Object owner SYNC_TO_EVAL|PARAMETERS. Native property flags do not mark Object.data NO_DEG_UPDATE. This whole assignment footprint, not setter pointer-change admission alone, determines paint-owner drain requirements.

BKE_mesh_assign_object only early-returns on nullObject. Even old==incomingMesh it calls multires_force_sculpt_rebuild, decrements/assigns/increments users, syncs materials and tests modifiers. Multires rebuild flushes sculpt updates then calls BKE_sculptsession_free_pbvh when sculpt exists; that resets PBVH/adjacency/boundary/topology caches. Thus same-pointer Mesh assignment has immediate storage effects in addition to late update; treating it as callback-free no-op is incorrect.

This demonstrates a possible evaluated-storage lifetime break under dependencies; it is not a device repro, deterministic scheduler trace or proof every assignment frees storage.
